events.title: The Sack of Rome and the stand of the Swiss Guard
events.shortBlurb: A mutinous imperial army stormed Rome, and the Pope's Swiss Guard died almost to a man defending him…
body: On 6 May 1527 the unpaid and mutinous troops of the Emperor Charles V, many of them German Lutheran mercenaries, broke into Rome and began a sack that lasted for days. Churches were plundered, relics desecrated, and the city ravaged in one of the worst catastrophes ever to befall it.

As the assault came, the Swiss Guard made its stand on the steps of St. Peter's so that Pope Clement VII might escape along the covered passage to the fortress of Castel Sant'Angelo. Of the guard, the greater part — by tradition one hundred forty-seven of one hundred eighty-nine — fell in the fighting. In memory of their sacrifice, new recruits of the Pontifical Swiss Guard are still sworn in on this day.
